title: Lace stole in Solomon's knot
subtitle: A long rectangular stole in Solomon's knot lace, worked in lace-weight cotton
excerpt: Solomon's knot is an elongated chain with a locking single crochet worked into the back loop, the result is an open, spiderweb lace fabric that uses very little yarn. This rectangular stole in lace-weight cotton is worked lengthwise, 200 cm long and 55 cm wide, on a 3 mm hook. The fabric is extremely light and drapes in long, fluid folds.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet chapter, Solomon's knot described as the "elongated loop with a locking stitch" and used for shawl borders and gossamer wraps. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 6 (1890), gives a full stole pattern in the same construction (Internet Archive).
heroPrompt: A fine lace stole in cream lace-weight cotton laid flat on a stone surface in bright daylight, the Solomon's knot lace pattern forms a regular open grid with small diamond spaces throughout.

glossaryTerms.definition: An elongated chain loop with a single locking double crochet worked into its back loop. The elongated chain creates the open mesh; the locking stitch anchors it. Also called the lover's knot.

content.text: A
Solomon's knot

stole is one of the lightest crochet wraps possible: the open mesh uses less than half the yarn of a solid-fabric stole of the same dimensions. This rectangular version in lace-weight cotton on a 3 mm hook finishes at 200 × 55 cm and folds into a very small bundle.

The stole is worked lengthwise along the 200 cm edge, which means the foundation row is long but each subsequent row adds depth quickly. The selvedge is neat: each row begins and ends with a standard double crochet (UK dc, the same move US patterns call single crochet) into the turning knot.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 150 g lace-weight cotton yarn (100% cotton works well; silk-cotton blend is also suitable). A 3 mm hook (US C/2 or D/3). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

4 Solomon's knot pairs × 8 rows = 10 × 10 cm in lace-weight cotton with a 3 mm hook, blocked flat. The gauge is measured after blocking; unblocked Solomon's knot lace is denser and does not reflect the finished dimensions.
How to work a Solomon's knot
Draw up the working loop to the height required by the pattern (here 1 cm). This is the elongated chain loop.
Identify the single strand running behind the elongated loop (the "back loop" of the elongated chain).
Insert the hook under this back strand only, yarn over, and draw through a loop (two loops on hook).
Yarn over, pull through both loops. This locking double crochet anchors the elongated loop.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
Solomon's knot (SK): elongated chain with a locking dc into the back loop.
Pattern
Abbreviations: SK = one Solomon's knot (elongated 1 cm loop + locking dc into back strand).
Foundation row

Work a foundation row of Solomon's knots to approximately 200 cm. The exact count is flexible; work an even number of SK pairs. Join the row by working 1 dc into the back loop of the second-to-last locking dc before the turning knot. This sets the first row of mesh.
Row 1
Turn. *Work 2 SK, skip the next locking dc, 1 dc into the next locking dc*; repeat from * to * across. 2 SK at end of row, 1 dc into the last locking dc of the foundation. Turn.
Rows 2 onward
Repeat Row 1 on each row. Continue until the stole measures 55 cm deep from the foundation row (approximately 44 rows at the given gauge). Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in the two ends. Wet-block by soaking in cool water for 15 minutes, pressing out gently, then pinning to the full 200 × 55 cm dimensions on a blocking mat. Solomon's knot lace opens significantly on blocking . Do not skip this step.
Care
Handwash in cool water only. Lay flat to dry on a towel. Do not press with a hot iron directly on cotton lace.
What to try next
Work the same construction in a silk-cotton blend for a softer drape suitable for evening wear. The same mesh pattern scales up to a beach cover-up in a chunky cotton tape yarn on a 5 mm hook.
